advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure seeded (cache-credited) criteria are re-attached to the verdict (and cache refreshed) on the primary-SUCCESS path, not only on the recovery/_finalize path.
evidence: completion_recovery.py:488-496: on primary success 'the bank is discarded unread' — `bank.discard()` then `result.outputs` used as-is; no seeded re-credit
completion_verdict_cache.py:276-277: directive 'Do not re-verify, re-investigate, or report on them' is appended to the primary context, so a compliant primary omits those criteria from its output
gate_ops.py:295 `result["criteria"] = list(ctx.inputs.get("raw_criteria") or [])` — reconcile carries the agent's criteria verbatim with no coverage backfill
completion.py:520 reconcile_verdict only normalizes verdict/findings; it performs no full-coverage check
merge_finalizer_with_bank (completion_verdict_assembly.py:176-188) — the ONLY place seeded entries are re-credited — runs solely on the recovery/_finalize path (completion_recovery.py:731)
advisory.finding: On the PRIMARY-SUCCESS path, criteria seeded from the cross-run cache are omitted from the primary manifest and the primary is instructed via seeded_context_block to 'not re-verify, re-investigate, or report on them'. When the primary run succeeds (does not exhaust), its structured output is used verbatim (bank.discard() at completion_recovery.py:489) and neither reconcile_verdict nor completion_reconcile backfills missing criteria. The seeded criteria therefore silently disappear from the emitted verdict, and the seeded-credit re-attach only happens on the recovery/_finalize path via merge_finalizer_with_bank.
scenarios: A prior run seeds PASS verdicts for some criteria; the next run's primary succeeds within budget and, obeying the directive, omits the seeded criteria — the final verdict loses coverage of those criteria (and the cache is not refreshed since persist runs only in _finalize).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether primary-SUCCESS verdicts should also persist to the cross-run cache; if so, wire persist_pass_verdicts into the primary-success path.
evidence: completion_recovery.py:735 `_cache.persist_pass_verdicts(ticket_id, merged, entries, self._repo_root)` is inside `_finalize`, reached only after recovery
completion_recovery.py:488-496 primary-success branch calls neither persist_pass_verdicts nor touches the cache
completion_verdict_cache.py:3-5 module docstring: 'persists each VALIDATED PASS record at finalize' — implies the successful path too
advisory.finding: On the PRIMARY-SUCCESS path, persist_pass_verdicts is never called (it only runs inside _finalize at completion_recovery.py:735). A run that succeeds on the primary and validated its criteria as PASS does not populate/refresh the cross-run cache, so the cache is only ever written by runs that went through exhaustion recovery — a narrower population than the design ('each VALIDATED PASS record is persisted at finalize') implies.
scenarios: A ticket verifies successfully on the primary without exhaustion; no cache entries are written, so a later re-verify cannot be accelerated even though a validated PASS existed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving _primary_manifest_contract with a bank + a seeded cached PASS, asserting the seeded id is omitted from the returned manifest, the 'already credited' directive is appended for it, and the bank entry is stamped seeded.
evidence: completion_recovery.py:527-532 seed_bank_from_cache(...) then primary_criteria_manifest(expected, id_by_text, seeded_ids=seeded) then manifest += _cache.seeded_context_block([...], id_by_text)
search for `_primary_manifest_contract` returns only src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py hits — no test file references it
tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_verdict_cache.py:297-319 test primary_criteria_manifest and seeded_context_block only as standalone helpers, never through _primary_manifest_contract
advisory.finding: The primary-manifest seeding seam _primary_manifest_contract (which composes seed_bank_from_cache, primary_criteria_manifest(seeded_ids=...), and seeded_context_block) has no test; only the three helpers are tested in isolation, so a regression in the wiring (e.g. failing to pass seeded_ids to the manifest, or passing the wrong text list to the directive block) would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor changes how seeded ids are threaded into the manifest; seeded criteria would be re-verified (defeating the cache) but all component tests still pass

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting _run_successors sizes the recovery pool with the ticket's direct-child count (childful epic yields a larger successor_pool than the equivalent childless ticket, and enumeration failure falls open to direct_children=0).
evidence: completion_recovery.py:637-641 plan_recovery_pool(len(expected), primary_spent, verify_cfg, direct_children=_cache.direct_child_count(ticket_id, self._repo_root))
commit message: 'plan_recovery_pool via its sole caller _run_successors' — named as the second fail-open consumer
search for `_run_successors` in tests/ returns (no matches)
tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py:87-113,116-153 exercise child sizing / fail-open only for the primary-sizing consumer in completion.py
advisory.finding: The recovery-pool consumer's child-term wiring is untested: _run_successors passes direct_children=_cache.direct_child_count(ticket_id, ...) into plan_recovery_pool, but no test exercises this call site — plan_recovery_pool(direct_children=) and direct_child_count fail-open are each tested only standalone.
scenarios: A change drops or miswires the direct_children argument at the recovery call site; the successor pool would be sized childlessly for epics, shrinking recovery budget, with no test failure

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_blob_shas` resolve absent-path blob SHAs without spawning one `git rev-parse` subprocess per path (e.g. batch via `git ls-tree`/`cat-file --batch-check` that reports missing entries inline, so cost stays O(1) subprocess calls regardless of file_impact path count).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py:105-112: `batched = _git_lines(repo_root, "rev-parse", *[f"HEAD:{path}" for path in paths])` ... `for path in paths: lines = _git_lines(repo_root, "rev-parse", f"HEAD:{path}")`

The batch is considered a failure when `proc.returncode != 0` (line 94) — a single absent path fails the whole batch per the docstring: `ANY absent path fails the whole batch`, making the per-path fallback a common, not rare, path.

Path list scales with user-controlled input: for an epic, `scoped_content_fingerprint` builds `child_paths = sorted({p for kid in children for p in _normalize_impact(kid.get("file_impact"))})` (lines 124-126), unioning all direct-child file_impact paths.
Each subprocess carries `timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` = 30 (line 90, constant at line 55 region), so worst-case latency also scales linearly.
scoped_content_fingerprint is invoked on both persist (line 168) and load (line 216), so the fallback loop can run twice per verification run.
advisory.finding: In `_blob_shas`, when the single batched `git rev-parse` fails (which occurs whenever ANY file_impact path is absent from HEAD), the fallback issues one `subprocess.run(git rev-parse ...)` per path — an N+1 subprocess-spawn pattern whose cost scales with the user-controlled file_impact path count (unbounded for an epic that unions all direct-child impact paths), each call carrying a 30s timeout ceiling.
scenarios: An epic ticket whose direct children collectively declare many file_impact paths, one of which was renamed/removed/not-yet-committed, so the batch rev-parse returns non-zero and every path is re-resolved via its own git subprocess.
A ticket with a large file_impact list where any single path is absent from HEAD.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the per-path fallback with a single batched resolution that tolerates missing paths in one process, e.g. feed all `HEAD:<path>` specs to `git cat-file --batch-check` (which emits `<spec> missing` lines for absent entries) so absent paths map to the sentinel without a per-path subprocess spawn.
